alex_chen: Heads up - after yesterday's kernel-selection rollout (auto-hint v2) we're seeing a host CPU increase on ingress preproc and a tail latency bump for streaming requests. p95 decode went from 18ms -> 33ms on canary. KV hit rate also dipped.
maria_g: ack, saw the alert. which routes are impacted? streaming vs non-streaming?
alex_chen: Mostly streaming paths (chat/generate). Quick snapshot from the canary window:

```
route=chat.stream  p95_host_preproc=33ms (prev 18ms)
kv_hit_rate=0.82 (prev 0.96)
grpc_writev_count/s=1200 -> 2200
cpu_user%_host_preproc=62 -> 78
```

samir: interesting that writev doubled. Could be fragmentation + new kernel picking a small-frame kernel leading to more syscalls.
tj: do we have traces? I want to check where the extra CPU cycles are spent (tokenize vs parse vs writev).
alex_chen: uploaded a short flame for the canary box: hotspots are: tokenizer::normalize (20%), host::grpc_writev_loop (18%), kv::evict_scan (12%). Link: https://perf.redwood/canary/1915
perfbot: Canary deploy "auto-hint-v2" started by @maria_g at 2026-03-18T09:12:45Z
maria_g: suspected root: kernel selector now prefers the "min-frame" kernel for medium sequence lengths which reduces GPU kernel throughput marginally but changes host framing behavior. That min-frame path trips our small-write path in the proxy which ends up with many small writev's and poor coalescing.
samir: that would also change buffering behavior in the pretokenizer. If pretokenizer emits smaller chunks, KV cache keys get less prefix overlap -> higher eviction rate.
alex_chen: hypothesis validated by trace: many requests produce 3-5 extra framing writes and shorter prefixes in kvcache keys. Also saw more memmove calls in tokenizer.
tj: quick mitigations:
- roll back kernel selector to "stable-v1" on canary hosts
- increase grpc sender buffer / enable writev coalescing in proxy (short-term)
- bump kvcache min-prefix to 64 bytes to avoid thrash

maria_g: agree. I'll flip the canary rollback now and open a PR for proxy coalesce. samir can you test kvcache prefix bump impact on memory?
samir: will run a small sim. ballpark: bumping min-prefix to 64 increases memory by ~1.8% in our load test but reduces eviction rate to ~0.95 hit rate.
alex_chen: sample proxy patch (quick PoC for coalescing):

```rust
// coalesce small writev fragments into a single buffer before writev
if pending_frag.len() < COALESCE_THRESH {
  temp_buf.extend_from_slice(pending_frag);
} else {
  flush_writev(&temp_buf);
}
```

maria_g: also consider pretokenizing at the edge (ingress proxy) as an opt-in: move normalization/strip to proxy threadpool so host sees fewer small tokens. But that adds CPU at edge.
tj: long-term fix ideas:
- teach kernel selector to consider host-framing cost (i.e., cost model include host write syscalls)
- adapt batching heuristic: min_batch_tokens should be dynamic based on current writev rate + kv_hit_rate
- KV cache key canonicalization to preserve longer shared prefixes even with different chunk boundaries

- alex_chen: instrument writev counts per route and add dashboard

samir: noted.

tj: will also add a tiny canary that forces pretokenize=true for 10% of traffic so we can measure edge CPU tradeoffs.
